title: Direct monitor joins added 4,183 US bird surveys without a clear ozone timing contrast in 1995-2023
abstract: We tested whether a requirement for a future bird survey changed an ozone timing test. We calculated future summer ozone directly from a verified public monitor table and original route coordinates. This added 4,183 surveys to a published US bird sample of 26,868 surveys in 1995-2023. It recovered 1,212 surveys from 2019. The new sample had 31,051 surveys. Four East and West, early and late models controlled weather, survey conditions, route, observer and regional annual effects. Prior-minus-future ozone slopes were +0.029, -0.475, -0.376 and -0.242 recorded species per 10 ppb. All four corrected intervals included zero. Trend and route-by-observer checks also gave uncertain contrasts. Added surveys had lower raw mean richness in all four samples. This does not establish slope bias. Direct monitor joins remove selection on a future bird record but retain selection on monitor coverage and complete current data. The test does not establish equal slopes, no ozone effect, or a causal climate effect. Code, source hashes, aggregate results, a figure and a separate numerical check are included. External input and record-level tables remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Direct monitor joins add 4,183 surveys. All four prior-minus-future ozone slope intervals include zero. Intervals use state clusters and a correction for four contrasts.

citations.reason: Verified panel, monitor table and source-build code.
Extends its time-order model by removing the future biological survey requirement. Shared observations; this is not independent data replication.
